report:
FRESH NONAUTHOR SECURITY SOURCE REVIEW. Requested model: claude-opus-5-5, high effort. I used the Read tool only. I did not execute, import, compile, hash or edit anything, and I made no shell, web, SDK, native, key or provider access. Every runtime statement below is a prediction. Byte counts and SHA-256 values are as declared by MANIFEST.json; I did not recompute them.

COVERAGE. I read all 14 manifest files completely. That includes the whole 1085-line candidate: Part A (lines 1-179), Part B (182-641), Part C (644-1085: helpers, all 18 methods and the main tail).

VERDICT: NOT READY ON THESE EXACT BYTES. There is one medium source fix (F1) and one low honesty fix (F2). Both change test bytes, so the RED should be observed on the corrected bytes, not on this frozen candidate. Apart from these, the source is careful and matches the contract closely. I found no defect that changes the predicted RED.

PREDICTED RED on the current bytes (unobserved):
- unittest collects 18 methods, test_T00 through test_T17. There are no extra test-prefixed helpers. T05a/b/c are subTest labels inside T05.
- setUpModule passes the pins: host 23252/3c18..., K6 5800/9301..., K2 SHA 86b5..., v1 15231/23c3....
- T00 never calls _prepare. Every T00 assertion holds against the S15/S16 literals: 12 setup keys, 29 relation keys split 13 consumed + 16 non-consumed, the 7 export object key sets, provenance values, HIST_ENV_CBOR segment framing, 16/8 labels, and TAMPER structure with BUILD empty.
- T01-T17 each call _prepare() as their first statement. os.open on the absent r2 raises FileNotFoundError, which becomes AssertionError(MISSING_R2). MISSING_R2 is byte-identical to the S33 section 7 phrase.
- Result: 1 pass, 17 failures carrying that phrase, 0 errors, exit 1.

PART A _prepare SCOPE (independent decision). The try block at lines 166-169 wraps the whole _read call (lines 91-104), not only the os.open at line 92. So, literally, the handler also covers fstat (94), os.read (98) and os.close (104). In _read, os.open sits outside the inner try/finally, and the ENOENT-capable step is that path-based open. fstat, read and close act on an already-open descriptor, and their documented Linux error sets do not include ENOENT. Non-regular files and oversize raise AssertionError without the phrase. A symlink fails under O_NOFOLLOW with ELOOP, not ENOENT. Other OSErrors, exec exceptions and a missing or non-function prepare_c2_issue all surface without the phrase. S33 section 7 itself requires 'the same _read' and also 'only FileNotFoundError from that exact open'.

My decision: the literal source satisfies the contract in operation, and no fix is required for this ROOT RED scope. As an optional tightening (F3), check error.filename against the r2 path. That keeps the same _read.

SETUP SIZE. T00 explicitly checks the setup byte size and SHA: lines 700 and 703 on the re-read, and line 704 on FIX['setup']. setUpModule (line 143) checks only the SHA, as v1 did. The SHA match implies byte identity, so this is info only.

LOADER AND EFFECTS.
- Bounded reads: os.open uses O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, then an fstat S_ISREG check, then a read loop that stops past the cap.
- exec uses compile(dont_inherit=True) into a fresh ModuleType. No r2 or v1 module is registered in sys.modules.
- sys.modules['host_codec']: installed in setUpModule, swapped to the proxy in T01 inside try/finally, and restored in tearDownModule. Under -I no script directory is on sys.path, so 'import host_codec' resolves only to the pinned module.
- Output: one stderr SHA line, emitted only when r2 is read.
- Hidden effects are info only:
  - unittest/linecache read source files with an ordinary open when they format tracebacks.
  - A FIFO in place of a fixture would block the open (no O_NONBLOCK). This relies on root pinning regular files.
  - If r2's exec raised, r2 would be re-read on every call.

TABLES AND CASES (each one checked against S11/S22/S15/S16):
- T02: the 6 expiry heads (2**32 is an 8-byte head, and 1893456000000 = 0x1b8dac5b400), 2 policies, HIST token literal, hashlib NON-ORACLE tokens for the other 5 expiries, 710-byte issue framing (7x64+40 VK, 3x64 proof, length 1420), mint framing, Data shapes, and equality of the four byte fields with v1.
- T03: list/None/str/_Hooked for both records, 6 expiry and 5 policy cases, and a check that records are untouched (dict.keys bypasses the hooks; dict(export) construction triggers no hook).
- T04: SETUP cases; the v1 ADMIT exceptions are exactly the driver one-char change and provingKeyBytes 2**64.
- T05: 34 T05a cases (v1 SETUP), 57 T05b cases (v1 ADMIT; includes all 12 logicalWork cases and the shape cases) and 1 T05c case (v1 RELATION).
- T06: every stage owner is correct. statementHex, proofHex and x1 keep their length, and the exact-ValueError assertion catches any UnicodeEncodeError leak.
- T07: 7 extra-key cases plus envV2 expiry; 49 missing-key cases; the 6 nested objects as lists; range cases; 8 bool cases (one per int field); action int; sourceSha256 'A'*64; 4 premises cases.
- T08/T10/T13: every replacement is type- and range-valid. Setup-side abi2ShapeDigest is correctly left to T05c.
- T09: flips at 0/16/48/80/112, truncation, and bodyLen 377.
- T11: x1 and x2 tampers are the str '0'.
- T12: correct.
- T14: all nine adjacent pairs with the literal v1 outcomes (SETUP/PROFILE v1 ADMIT, PROFILE/EXPORT v1 EXPORT). No BUILD negative case is invented.
- T16: exactly the 65 S34 T16StrictnessCases. T02/T17 are excluded, and every case checks /1 plus the exact 8 labels.
- T17: uses HIST_EXPIRY and HIST_POLICY explicitly and changes all five context fields at offsets 144/173/233/265/267, with networkId staying 0. It closes the digest, x1/x2, envV2 claimant/settleOutref/statementDigest and intentAnchor dependencies. proofHex is unchanged. Env is literal framing and the token is the NON-ORACLE hashlib value, labelled SYNTHETIC_NOT_PROOF_NOT_ORACLE. It makes no Rust, proof or ledger claim.
- T01: checks the import lines, the signature, the namespace and that all 7 host APIs are counted by the proxy, then restores sys.modules.

DISSENT AND LIMITS.
- F1 (medium): T15's global-state baseline is taken only after T01-T14 have already called r2 with the very same inputs. A content-keyed cache, or any in-place module-container mutation that settles after its first use, therefore cannot be detected, although CP07 forbids caching and global mutation.
- F2 (low): the module docstring still calls the file a 'PART A prefix'. It also says no expected token or digest comes from a production hash call, which contradicts the hashlib NON-ORACLE expectations in Part B, T02 and T17.
- What stays with later source inspection: the CP04 constraints (no str.encode, no input-proportional copy, length before scan), the CP01 alias and no-reimplementation rules, and caching in non-container state. T15 states this honestly.
- v1 and shared-host equality is consistency, not an oracle. Rust acceptance, proof validity and ledger facts are not established.
- The envelope matches section 7 (10 s, 512 MiB, fsize 2 MiB, core 0, clearenv, --unshare-all with no network, read-only /usr and /input, exactly the five RED files). It is acceptable for a later RED of corrected, re-reviewed bytes. Notes: the bwrap root is an ephemeral writable tmpfs (--remount-ro / is optional), and ROOT_PINNED_555_ENVELOPE is a template placeholder that root must fill.
- No runtime is authorized. This review is scoped to its frozen packet. It makes no claim about other lib.rs or Sherlock modules. It is a same-provider fresh context, not provider diversity. The model identity is self-reported.

findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:946-1001 (test_T15_detachment_nonaliasing_and_source_effects). The names, identities and deep-copied container state snapshots (lines 949-954) are taken from FIX['r2'] only when T15 starts. unittest runs methods in name order, so T02-T14 have already called FIX['prepare'] hundreds of times by then. T15's success input is the same fresh K6 input T02 uses (line 958; T02 lines 815-817), and its refusal inputs are exactly T14_CASES + CASE_CARDANO_ANCHOR (line 981), already used in T14 (line 938) and T13 (lines 588-605). An r2 that mutates a module-level dict/list in place on first use (for example a content-keyed memo of VK digests or statement headers) would be warm before the snapshot. T15's state comparison (lines 989-994) and the held-container checks (lines 995-998) would then pass. The 'global' token scan (lines 250 and 1007-1009) catches only rebinding. S33 CP07 forbids caching and global mutation, and the T15 row requires 'module namespace keys and mutable globals unchanged'.
findings.requiredFix: In T15, after the leading _prepare() call, exec a fresh r2 module from FIX['r2_bytes'] with _module against the pinned FIX['host'] (sys.modules unchanged, no proxy; T01 sets the precedent). Take the names/identities/container-state snapshot of that fresh module before its first call, and route every T15 success and refusal call through the fresh module's prepare_c2_issue. Keep _prepare() as T15's first statement. Then re-freeze the bytes and obtain a fresh review of the changed bytes before any root RED. Caching in non-container state stays a source-inspection obligation.

findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:1-13. The docstring calls the file an 'Author-proposed PART A prefix' (now stale: the file is the combined Part A+B+C). It also says 'every expected digest, token and CBOR byte is a public literal, or literal framing around pinned fixture bytes, never a call to a production hash or encoder'. That conflicts with Part B lines 183-189 and _token (285-287), T02 lines 810 and 823 (hashlib.blake2b token expectations), and T17 lines 1037 and 1062 (hashlib statement digest and token). These are the same hashlib.blake2b primitive the v1 consumer uses (S11 line 336). The Part B and inline comments label them NON-ORACLE correctly; the docstring does not.
findings.requiredFix: Update the module docstring to describe the whole combined file. State that the only computed expectations are the S33 section 6 hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32) NON-ORACLE token values over literal envCborHex, plus the T17 SYNTHETIC_NOT_PROOF_NOT_ORACLE statement digest and x1/x2. Note that they are independent of host_codec but not of hashlib, and that v1 equality is shared-host consistency, not an oracle. Make this edit in the same revision as F1.

findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:160-169 catches FileNotFoundError around the whole _read(R2_FILE, 131072) call. _read (lines 91-104) runs os.open at line 92 outside its inner try/finally, then fstat (94), os.read (98) and os.close (104) on the open descriptor. S33 section 7 requires both 'r2 is read by the same _read' and 'Only FileNotFoundError from that exact open'. On Linux only the path-based open can raise ENOENT: O_NOFOLLOW symlinks give ELOOP, non-regular files and oversize raise AssertionError without the phrase at lines 95 and 102, and other errors propagate. The comment at lines 161-164 matches this effective behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: No fix is required for the reviewed ROOT RED scope; the contract is satisfied operationally. Optional tightening in the F1/F2 revision: inside the except clause, re-raise unless error.filename == os.path.join(HERE, R2_FILE). A descriptor-level error carries filename None, so only the exact r2 open can then produce MISSING_R2, and the same _read is kept.

findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:1003-1005 disclaims honestly that the CP04 constraints are not discriminated. T01 lines 754-756 scan for imports by line prefix only, so a mid-line '; import' is not caught. Lines 768-770 bar only exact host API names from the namespace: a privately named alias or a parallel re-implementation is not detected, and the counts at lines 801-803 prove only that each API is called at least once. '.encode(' is not among EFFECT_TOKENS (line 246; optional per S42 R4-L02).
findings.requiredFix: None for the test. The later r2 implementation review must source-inspect: no str.encode, no input-proportional copy, length before scan, host APIs used only as host_codec attributes with no re-implementation, no caching in any state, and imports only as the two allowed statements.

findings.evidence: T01 line 771-774 rejects any public callable (classes included), which is stricter than the CP01 wording 'only public function'. EFFECT_TOKENS (line 250) includes 'global', so the r2 source cannot contain the word even in a docstring (for example 'global mutation' copied from CP07). Both are consistent with S33 (the T15 row says 'plus global').
findings.requiredFix: None. Implementation guidance: define no public classes or other public callables, and keep the word 'global' out of the r2 text.

findings.evidence: PROPOSED-ORDINARY-ENVELOPE.json argvTemplate: --unshare-all (new net namespace), --ro-bind /usr and --ro-bind ROOT_PINNED_555_ENVELOPE /input, --clearenv plus PATH/LANG/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, prlimit cpu 10, as 536870912, fsize 2097152, core 0, timeout 10s with kill-after 2s, python3 -I -B. This matches S33 section 7. The bwrap root is an ephemeral writable tmpfs: it is discarded and the test writes nothing (-B, dont_write_bytecode). ROOT_PINNED_555_ENVELOPE is a placeholder. _read opens without O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO would block; this is bounded by the timeout and excluded by root pinning regular 0444 files. A malicious r2 could raise text containing MISSING_R2, but r2 is absent at RED.
findings.requiredFix: None blocking. When root later admits corrected and re-reviewed bytes: substitute only the placeholder with a 0555 directory holding exactly the five pinned 0444 files, observe r2 absence before the run, and optionally add --remount-ro / . A phrase is accepted only with r2 absence observed by root.

recommendation.ordinarySelftestScope: NONE for the frozen bytes 9b539d7d566daa8b3790b7e7cd685a45c33f18619127dc0c01adbe1ef07cf599. After the F1 (and F2) corrections are re-frozen and freshly reviewed, the only scope that could be considered is one ROOT RED: the PROPOSED-ORDINARY-ENVELOPE argv with only ROOT_PINNED_555_ENVELOPE substituted by a 0555 directory holding exactly the five pinned 0444 files (test, host_codec.py, c2_issue_artifacts.py, K6-PUBLIC-PROOF.json, K2-PUBLIC-SETUP-RECORD.json), r2 absence observed by root, run once with no retry. Predicted outcome: 18 methods, T00 pass, T01-T17 MISSING_R2 failures, 0 errors. No GREEN, mutants, broad suites, implementation or native action.
recommendation.firstBlockedBoundary: F1: T15 takes its global-state and namespace baseline only after T01-T14 have already called r2 with the identical inputs, so in-place caching or global mutation of module containers that settles after first use cannot be detected (CP07). A corrected, re-frozen test revision (with the F2 docstring correction) plus a fresh non-author review of the changed bytes must come before any root RED.

CPython behaviour (unittest method ordering and testsRun, json parse_constant and object_pairs_hook, dict-subclass construction without hooks, -I sys.path isolation, the ENOENT surface of open versus fd syscalls, int digit limits) and bwrap/prlimit/timeout semantics are stated from language and OS knowledge, not observed.

All RED and GREEN outcomes are predictions; no runtime is authorized by this review.
